summary: Iteration 9 — Email notification system verified end-to-end. Created /app/backend/tests/test_email_delivery_notification.py (8 tests, 100% pass). Confirmed: creating a delivery request via POST /api/delivery-requests triggers send_notification_email which successfully sends to ADMIN_EMAIL=badiroumounif@gmail.com (the Resend verified sender). Backend logs show 'INFO - Email sent successfully: 🚚 Livraison GOLIV-2026-000071 - TEST_EmailNotif_Client' and 'GOLIV-2026-000072 - TEST_EmailGraceful' — both from this run. Direct unit call to send_notification_email(to=verified_owner) returned True; call with unverified recipient returned False (graceful failure, no exception propagation).
critical_code_review_comments: send_notification_email (server.py L343-370) correctly (a) short-circuits when RESEND_API_KEY or recipient missing (returns False + WARNING), (b) wraps resend.Emails.send in try/except and returns False on any Exception, (c) logs 'Email sent successfully: {subject}' at INFO level on happy path — this is exactly the contract the test verifies.

POST /api/delivery-requests (L729-788) awaits send_notification_email but the endpoint still returns 200 regardless of email outcome — the return value is discarded and no HTTPException is raised. Graceful failure verified.
resend.Emails.send is executed via asyncio.to_thread — non-blocking. Good pattern.

Recommendation (non-blocking): consider spawning email sends as fire-and-forget background tasks (asyncio.create_task or FastAPI BackgroundTasks) instead of awaiting inline. Currently, when Resend is slow (~1-2s per call), the POST response is delayed by that much. Not a functional bug — just latency.
